excerpt: Compare Jumeirah Village Circle and Arjan apartment investments using the building, tenant needs, acquisition cost, service charges and net rent.
introduction:
Jumeirah Village Circle (JVC) and Arjan are both Dubai apartment markets worth comparing at the level of an individual building and unit. The choice depends on what you pay, the lease evidence, service charges, future competition and the way a tenant uses the location. An area-wide advertised yield cannot decide the investment for you.

This guide sets out a like-for-like method. The figures below provide a worked comparison of purchase costs and annual income in two scenarios.
takeaways: Compare the precise building, layout, parking and route to the tenant's likely destinations.
Use recent comparable leases and the unit's approved service charges to estimate net income.
Check ownership, project registration, construction and competing supply before committing.

sections.heading: Understand the two locations
sections.body:
[Property Finder's JVC guide](https://www.propertyfinder.ae/en/area-insights/dubai/jumeirah-village-circle) describes a community with apartments and a mix of other homes, parks and retail. Its [Arjan guide](https://www.propertyfinder.ae/en/area-insights/dubai/arjan) describes a mixed-use area with residential buildings near Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Umm Suqeim Road. These descriptions provide context; they do not establish the condition or performance of a specific tower.

Visit the exact addresses, check the entrance and parking, and test routes at times the intended tenant would travel. Ask about nearby construction, shops and access to public transport. A building's position and management may matter more than a broad neighbourhood description.

The [Dubai market guide](/journal/dubai-property-market-2026) provides wider context for comparing alternatives, while this guide focuses on JVC and Arjan.

sections.heading: Inspect the building and likely tenant fit
sections.body:
Identify the apartment's usable layout, bedroom size, storage, noise, cooling and the condition of the common areas. Check the allocated parking and the actual facilities rather than relying on a project-wide advertisement. For an off-plan apartment, review the contracted specifications, floor plan, payment milestones and handover provisions.

Consider the likely tenant's work, school and daily travel. Ask whether public transport and nearby services work from the specific building. A short distance on a map can involve a different route or junction in practice. Test the journey and record what is open today rather than assuming a planned amenity has been completed.

Look at comparable rental supply in and around the building. More competing units can affect the time needed to let or the rent achieved, although the effect cannot be predicted from a project count alone.

sections.heading: Calculate total cost and service charges
sections.body:
Add the purchase price, registration and brokerage costs, financing fees where relevant, initial repairs and furnishing. Obtain a current written quotation for the specific transaction. Keep a separate reserve for vacancy and unexpected work. Compare apartments on the same financing basis.

Dubai Land Department's [service charge index](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/service-charge-index/) provides a way to check approved community service charges. Ask the management for the unit statement, applicable area basis, arrears and what services are included. A building's charge can differ from another in the same area.

For a ready unit, check title, seller authority, tenancy and any mortgage. For a new project, verify the registered project, developer, payment recipient and the agreement. Ask DLD to confirm the ownership right and process for your particular unit.

sections.heading: Compare net rental income
sections.body:
Suppose a sample JVC apartment requires AED 1,000,000 in total acquisition cost and yields AED 50,000 in annual net operating income after vacancy and owner costs. A sample Arjan alternative requires AED 900,000 and yields AED 43,200 net. Their respective net operating yields are 5% and 4.8%. These example figures show how to compare costs and yields using the same calculation for each home.

Use recent signed leases for apartments comparable in size, furnishing, parking and condition. Subtract vacancy, the owner's service charges, management, repairs and insurance from expected rent. Divide by the full acquisition cost; keep finance and sale costs separate.

The chart shows the example only. Test a lower rent or higher charge and do not infer that either neighbourhood is generally superior from two sample cases.

sections.heading: Test the exit and the unknowns
sections.body:
Look for recent completed sales of comparable apartments as well as current competing listings. Compare asking prices with recent completed sales and the terms of similar properties. Allow for selling costs, remaining loan and the possibility of a longer sale period.

Check how many nearby buildings are scheduled for handover and whether their units compete with yours. Scheduled supply may be delayed or altered; it is not proof of future vacancy or price changes. Inspect the developer's track record and the individual project's progress where available.

Write down the uncertainties that matter most and the evidence needed to resolve each one. A property that fails your budget, ownership or condition requirements should not qualify merely because an advertised yield looks attractive.

sections.heading: Check the payment timeline
sections.body:
For an off-plan unit, write every instalment date and the conditions attached to it, including the amount due at handover and any payments afterwards. Compare the schedule with your available cash and a possible delay. Ask the developer how construction progress is reported and verify the registered project and payment arrangements independently.

For a ready unit, include the timing of the deposit, loan approval if required and transfer charges. A similar headline price can require very different cash at different points. Do not count an expected future rental income until the apartment can legally be occupied and the costs of letting have been considered.

sections.heading: Explore current opportunities
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas JVC projects](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-jvc) and [Arjan projects](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-arjan), then ask which exact units are currently available. Request a plan, price, payment terms and current building charges for each option.

[Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, intended tenant and holding period. Verify the project, official charges and ownership documents before making a commitment.
